chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about a man whose slave married a free woman, so he said: The divorce is in the hand of the slave. So if he married her without the permission of his master, then the divorce is in the hand of the master.
ai.seo_question: Who has the right to divorce a slave who married a free woman without his master's permission?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'taliq' (conditional divorce) within the master-slave dynamic, establishing that the master's grant of permission to marry also grants the slave autonomous authority over the dissolution of that union. It highlights the juristic principle that the master retains residual control only when the marriage occurred without his consent, reflecting the socio-legal hierarchy of early Islamic society. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining who holds the right to initiate talaq in cases of enslaved individuals.
